Notes and Assumptions:
1)  LPP proactive replacement capital expenditures in base rates total $77.375 million in CY 2017, $87.189 million in CY 2018 and $88.933 million in CY 2019.    
      Revenue requirement assumes capital expenditures are placed in-service in the month spent.
2)  Depreciation is based on the Depreciation Study recommended composite depreciation rate for mains and services based on 12/31/2015 plant balances.
3)  Utilizes pre-tax WACC by calendar year
4)  The amount subject to surcharge is limited to the Company's average costs of main replacement for comparable pipe materials, sizes, strata (e.g., pavement, grass) and working conditions
      (subject to inflation and other reasonable adjustments (e.g., new permitting requirements)).
5)  The CY 2017 incremental mileage spend will be rolled forward to the CY 2018 and CY 2019 surcharges, calculating a return on the net plant investment and associated depreciation expense. 
6)  The CY 2018 incremental mileage spend will be rolled forward to the CY 2019 surcharge, calculating a return on the net plant investment and associated depreciation expense. 
The final revenue requirement should be adjusted to incorporate any changes to the capital investment, depreciation rates, pre-tax WACC or opex approved in this case.

DPS-189, Attachment 3 does not agree with what is excluded from Exhibit, RRP-2,

6. For KEDNY, the tab “Normalizing Expense” in attachment file include with the
Companies’ response, DPS-189 Attachment 1, showcases expenses that should have
followed the same criteria used in normalizing Employee Expenses based on Exhibit,
RRP-2, Schedule 1, p. 3 of 8 (Summary of Test Year Employee Expense Adjustments
Receiving by Expense Type). Provide an explanation for:
i. The criteria used to normalize these expenses;
ii. The methodology used to ensure that the population of expenses
excluded was completely based on the criteria used; and
iii. Confirm that the listing of expenses should have been appropriately
excluded during normalization of expenses for both KEDNY and
KEDLI, and the updated amount due to normalization.
Response:
1. Please see Attachment 1 for a reconciliation and explanation of the differences
between DPS-189 and RRP-2, Schedule 1, p.3 of 8.
The differences are due to a
mapping issue between RRP-2 and RRP-3. In addition, certain expenses in RRP-2
had already been removed from the HTY, while others were inadvertently doubled in
the exhibit. The result is a decrease in the original adjusted amount of $38,989.97 to
$22,608.62. KEDNY will reflect this change in Corrections and Updates.
2. Please see Attachment 2 for a reconciliation and explanation of the differences
between DPS-189 and RRP-2, Schedule 1, p.3 of 8 for Band A related expenses. The
differences are due to a mapping issue between RRP-2 and RRP-3, a row of data that
Exhibit_____(RRP-11CU) 
Workpapers to Exhibit RRP-3CU 
Schedule 4 
Workpaper 3 
Page 2 of 4 
133


--- Page 141 ---
Form 103
was inadvertently not included in the adjustments, and certain expenses that were
incurred outside the HTY, but inadvertently included in the adjustments. The result is
an increase in the original adjusted amount of $15,579.69 to $23,113.67 in DPS-189.
KEDNY will reflect this change in Corrections and Updates.
3. Please see Attachment 3 for a reconciliation and explanation of the differences
between DPS-189 and RRP-2, Schedule 1, p.3 of 8.
The differences are due to a
mapping issue between RRP-2 and RRP-3 and a minor rounding issue. In addition,
certain expenses in RRP-2 had already been removed from the HTY, while others
were inadvertently doubled in the exhibit.
The result is a decrease in the original
adjusted amount of $22,004.19 to $18,458.01. KEDLI will reflect these changes in
Corrections and Updates.
4. Please see Attachment 4 for a reconciliation and explanation of the differences
between DPS-189 and RRP-2, Schedule 1, p.3 of 8 for Band A related expenses. The
differences are due to a mapping issue between RRP-2 and RRP-3 and an expense
that was incurred outside the HTY, but inadvertently included in the adjustments.
The result is an increase in the original adjusted amount of $9,490.66 to $14,294.76.
KEDLI will reflect this change in Corrections and Updates
5. Please see Attachments 5 and 6, for KEDLI and KEDNY, respectively, for copies of
all expense reports and related receipts. Also, please see Attachments 7 and 8, for
KEDLI and KEDNY, respectively, which break out the allocation of the total expense
between companies and also explains why the charges are appropriate.
6. The Companies undertook an extensive analysis to normalize employee expenses.
i.
As described in the testimony of the Revenue Requirements Panel, PwC
sampled employee expenses originating from the Companies and the Service
Company.
The Companies supplemented PwC’s review with a keyword
search of employee expenses incurred in the HTY. The keyword search was
applied to the “Trip Reason” of the population to examine expenses that
required further review. If the expense was determined to be excluded, the
Companies removed the expense in RRP-2, Schedule 1.
ii.
The Companies ensured that the population of expenses excluded was
completely based on the criteria described in (i.) above by searching the entire
population set and reviewing all generated results for KEDLI and KEDNY.
iii.
The “Normalizing Expense” tab in Staff’s attachment to DPS-257 reflects
categories of expenses that are different than the words and phrases used by
the Companies in their keyword search. For example, the category “Diversity
Club Events” was not a keyword used by the Companies.
Instead, the
Companies used the keyword “event” to search the population of expenses. If
“event” showed up in “Trip Reason,” the Companies normalized the expense.
This was a conservative approach that, as discussed below, resulted in many
employee expenses being excluded that should have been included. In some
Exhibit_____(RRP-11CU) 
Workpapers to Exhibit RRP-3CU 
Schedule 4 
Workpaper 3 
Page 3 of 4 
134


--- Page 142 ---
Form 103
cases, because every form of a word could not be captured, certain expenses
were missed.
These will be removed, as discussed below.
The foregoing
explains why some expenses are included or excluded in the categories listed
in Staff’s attachment.
Attachment 9 contains a list of expenses that should not have been normalized
from the HTY, together with certain expenses that the Companies agree to
remove. The “Comment” column explains the reason for the adjustment. The net
result is a $1,236.18 in additional expenses to exclude for KEDNY, and a net
result of $78.21 to include for KEDLI. The Companies will reflect this change in
Corrections and Updates.

Request:
1. Referring to exhibit RRP-3 Schedule 9 Page 6; for each new project included in this
schedule, for both KEDNY and for KEDLI provide the following:
a.
A description of the project;
b. The related cost benefits analysis supporting the Company’s position to pursue the
project;
c.
The actual costs incurred to date, as well as cost(s) forecasted through the rate year,
broken down by cost component; and
d. The term of the amortization period, as well as a detailed explanation for why this term
has been chosen.
2. Referring to exhibit RRP-3 Schedule 9 Page 6; for each project listed on lines 16 to 35 and
for each project over $50,000 that is included in line 36 provide the sanction paper that
supports the project for both KEDNY and for KEDLI. If there is no sanction paper, provide
a detailed explanation why not.
3. Referring to exhibit RRP-3 Schedule 9 Page 7; provide a detailed explanation why the
existing facilities projects are included in Service Company Rents instead of being included
in Rent Expense for both KEDNY and for KEDLI.
4. Referring to exhibit RRP-3 Schedule 9 Page 7; for each new project included in this
schedule, for both KEDNY and for KEDLI provide the following:
a.
A description of the project;

Form 103
b. The related cost benefits analysis supporting the Company’s position to pursue the
project;
c.

broken down by cost component; and
d. The term of the amortization period, as well as an explanation for why this term has been
chosen.
Response:
1. a. Please see Attachment 1 to DPS-225 for project descriptions.
b. Information Services (“IS”) projects are undertaken for a number of reasons such as meeting
legal or regulatory requirements, maintaining IS system reliability, addressing loss of vendor or
version support, or providing service enhancements. Although IS projects can enable economic
benefits, many projects are selected for other factors. Discussion of benefits and project costs
are standard elements of IS sanction papers. For each new project listed on Exhibit RRP-3
Schedule 9 Page 6, the Companies are providing copies of the sanction papers, which include
discussions of each respective project’s benefits and costs. In the event a project was re-
sanctioned, due to a change in schedule or cost, the original sanction paper and the re-sanction
paper have been provided.
The Hub Drive Security enhancements project did not have a sanction paper as it is
facilities-related and the governance process of National Grid’s Facilities department does not
require a sanction paper for projects under $1 million. The work was approved under the
Delegation of Authority (DOA) process. The project is the result of a security and resilience
review at the new Melville gas service operations site that identified the need for a number of
security improvements. The security and resilience report, included in Attachment 21 to DPS-
225 as support for the business case, was presented to and approved by senior management.
The benefits for this initiative, as noted in Attachment 1 to DPS-225, are to upgrade the physical
security at the site in support of the move of Gas Service Operations to that location. This
project will be moved from the IS page to the Facilities page in Schedule 9 in the Company’s
Corrections and Updates Filing. Please note that Attachment 21 to DPS-225 contains critical
infrastructure information and has been redacted for this response. The original version of the
attachment is being provided separately pursuant to a request for protection from disclosure.

*Refers to which Company’s Schedule 9, Page 6 of RRP-3 the project is listed in.
c. Please see Attachment 33 to DPS-225, which provides actual project costs by cost component
through September 2015 and total project forecast cost through the Rate Year for each new
project identified in Exhibit __ (RRP-3), Schedule 9, page 6. It is not the Company’s practice to
forecast by individual cost component; therefore, forecast information at that level of detail is not
available. Also, please note that the project forecast amounts through the Rate Year reflect the
amounts included in Exhibit __ (RRP-11), Workpapers to Exhibit __ (RRP-3), Schedule 9,
Workpaper 2. Forecasts reflect the best available information to the Company at the time the
forecast was made. However, as the project progresses, actual costs may differ from forecasts
due to changes in scope. Although actual costs after September 2015 for any individual project
may exceed the corresponding forecast for that project, at this time, the Companies do not
anticipate revising the overall aggregate total forecast for New/Forecasted Projects as shown in
Exhibit __ (RRP-3), Schedule 9, page 6.
d. The amortization period for each project can be found in Exhibit __ (RRP-11), Workpapers to
Exhibit __ (RRP-3), Schedule 9, Workpaper 2 (Column “(f) Amortization Period”). The
amortization terms that were applied are based on the replacement cycle for the particular asset
type. The amortization period is dictated by plant accounting rules that are specific to each type
of asset. Recovery of hardware and equipment and amortization of software intangible assets
will approximate the useful life of the new system, taking into consideration technological and
functional obsolescence and vendor support options. For example, based on experience, the
Companies typically replace software applications every 84 months often to coincide with the
release of new version by the vendor, whereas, personal computers and laptops typically have a
useful life of 48 months.

3. The existing facilities projects are included in Service Company Rents instead of the Rent
Expense for KEDNY and KEDLI because these are facilities owned by the service company that
are used to provide services to multiple operating companies, including KEDNY and KEDLI.
The service company charges the operating companies a return on and of the assets it owns in a
manner similar to that by which a regulated utility includes a return on and of the utility plant
included in its rate base. The asset recovery charge is billed as rent expense to the operating
companies and is comprised of the following elements: depreciation, property tax, equity
component of return and debt component of return.
4. a. Please see Attachment 34 to DPS-225 for a description of the new facilities projects.
b. Many of the new facilities projects do not undergo a formal cost benefit analysis as the
projects are deemed mandatory to maintain building code and provide a safe workplace. These
projects include and are not limited to new roofs, plumbing, fixing of deteriorating pavement,
security and fire alarm systems and minor upgrades such as carpeting and doors.
c. Please see Attachment 34 to DPS-225 for additional information on incurred costs to date and
forecast costs. The current costs incurred are primarily comprised of labor and materials.
d. The amortization period for each project can be found in Exhibit __ (RRP-11), Workpapers to
Exhibit __ (RRP-3), Schedule 9, Workpaper 3 (Column “(e) Amortization Period”). The
amortization terms that were applied are based on the replacement cycle for the particular asset
type. The amortization period is dictated by plant accounting rules that are specific to each type
of asset. For the amortization period, a 120 month period was chosen as it follows how past
company facilities’ and leasehold improvements have been amortized.

SUBJECT:
SUSTAINABILITY HUB
Request:
1. Provide a detailed description and breakdown of the costs KEDNY would incur in
building a Sustainability Hub in its MetroTech office in Brooklyn (currently estimated at
$1.5 million), and in reconfiguring the office. Include a breakdown of the projected
expenditures for each phase of construction.
2. Provide a timeline for completion of the project, including an estimated date of
completion.
3. Include the projected annual expenditures for the Sustainability Hub for the three years
after its estimated date of completion.
4. Explain in detail the process and/or analyses supporting the proposal to build the
Sustainability Hub at this location. Include the following:
a.
All relevant studies and documentation; and
b. All cost/benefit analyses regarding this location, as well as, those analyses for any
other location that was considered for this project.
5. Provide a detailed outline of the activities, programs, and resources that will be offered at
the Sustainability Hub. Include a detailed calendar or project plan for these activities and
program, as well as, any resources offered by the Hub for the three years after the
estimated date of completion of the Sustainability Hub.

6. Explain in detail if, and how, these activities, programs, and resources offered by the Hub
will differ from those currently accessible at existing customer offices or through other
Company channels.
Response:
1. The cost of renovating and furnishing the 3,600 square feet of space is estimated at $1.5m or
approximately $415 per square foot. This estimate is based on similar projects completed, with
an increase for NYC construction costs.
Breakdown of Project Costs
Design, Engineering, construction
administration and project
management
$300,000
Temporary reconfiguration 2x
$100,000
Construction including furniture,
fixtures and equipment,
commissioning and testing
$1,100,000
Total
$1,500,000
The project will be constructed in two phases to allow a portion of the customer office to remain
functioning during renovation. Each phase of the project will have a demolition, construction,
commissioning, testing and relocation component.
The demolition portion of the work consists of removing the existing furniture, fixtures and
equipment and demolishing the interior walls to prepare for the renovations. Demolition includes
removal and disposal of carpet, lighting, and ceiling, ductwork for HVAC and associated wiring
and fire alarm system.
The new space will then be constructed. Construction entails carpentry, electrical, voice, data,
HVAC (including duct work), controls wiring, fire alarm and sprinkler work. Once completed
and accepted by the jurisdiction having authority (JHA), the furniture, fixtures and equipment
can be installed.
All new systems require commissioning and testing to confirm they meet the design
requirements. Commissioning is typically performed by a commissioning agent. Testing is
performed by all trades and the user group.
Once the first phase is completed, relocation of a portion of the customer office will take place
and phase two of construction can occur.

2. The project is anticipated to begin between the end of 2016 and early 2017 and take eight to
ten months to complete, once approved. Please note that in Exhibit RRP-3, Schedule 9, the
Company had initially assumed a December 31, 2016 in service date. This will be corrected in
the Company’s Correction and Updates filing.
3. Because the Sustainability Hub will be combined into the renovated customer office space, the
facilities lease and O&M cost associated with the facility is expected to remain unchanged from
the cost of the current MetroTech customer office, with the exception of increases for inflation.
Two interns will be hired to work the Sustainability Hub at an anticipated total cost of $18,720 in
calendar year 2017 and $37,440 in calendar year 2018 and on.
4.
a. The Company’s desire to build a Sustainability Hub is based in part on the success of our
existing Sustainability Hub located in Worcester MA (see, attachment 1 - National Grid’s Report
on the Smart Energy Solutions Sustainability Hub submitted in D.P.U. 11-129) coupled with a
desire to promote and educate our customers on gas safety, energy conservation and
sustainability. In addition, building a Sustainability Hub provides an opportunity to partner with
local colleges to create internships and foster interest in careers in energy.
b. The only NYC customer office considered for the Sustainability Hub was the Metrotech
location. The Metrotech location was selected because of its prime downtown Brooklyn
location. The Metrotech customer office has a significant storefront in a high pedestrian area to
display products and draw customers inside. Metrotech is accessible by multiple subway lines
and bus routes making it the most accessible of our four NYC walk-in customer offices. The
associated costs are outlined in the responses to questions 1-3 and included in the revenue
requirement in Exhibit RRP-3, Schedule 9, Page 7 and RRP-3, Schedule 27, Page 4.
5. Activities, programs and resources offered would be similar to those provided in the
Worcester location referenced in Attachment 1 with a focus on gas safety rather than smart-grid.
If approved, the Company plans to engage local colleges to partner with the Company to design
exhibits and interactive displays to educate customers on natural gas benefits and safety. For
example, the Company would provide “scratch and sniff” demonstrations to help customers
identify the odor of natural gas, give safety briefings on what to do if a gas leak is suspected and
build awareness around the importance of reporting concerns immediately. The Company also
plans to incorporate displays that demonstrate how to conserve energy use, demonstrate the use
of programmable thermostats, and provide information on how to select high efficiency gas
appliances.
As this initiative has not yet been approved, no formal calendar has been developed as of this
date.
6. The Sustainability Hub will differ from current channels because it is intended to be a hands-
on walk-in interactive learning environment. While information is available today in print and on
the phone and web, there is currently no place that a customer can visit in person to get
instructions on how to use a programmable thermostat, ask questions on gas safety, appliance

customers inside and engage them in learning about natural gas.
